newsitem.title: INDIA: WPP's O&M buying another Indian agency.
newsitem.headline: WPP's O&M buying another Indian agency.

text.p: NEW DELHI, June 5 (REUTER) - Ogilvy & Mather Worldwide (OMW), part of the British advertising and marketing concern WPP Group, said it had reached agreement to acquire Bombay-based Speer Advertising.
OMW has a 51 percent stake in Ogilvy & Mather India (O&M) , the country's third largest advertising agency.
Speer will remain a separate agency from O&M India, O&M said in a statement issued on Friday.
O&M India notched capitalised billings of $88.2 million in 1996/97 according to a report last month by the U.S. based Advertising Age.
Speer's billings totalled 200 million rupees ($5.5 million) in 1996/97, the Business Standard daily reported on Saturday.
The newspaper said O&M had agreed to take an 80 percent stake in Speer, but gave no price details.
It said the remaining 20 percent was retained by Speer.

"I have been looking for a partner of international stature and creative compatibility. O&M Worldwide offers both of these," Sajid Peerbhoy, Speer's founder, said in a statement announcing the signing of a memorandum of understanding for the aquisition.
